description: MLP gate/up: F-D2 (the multiply written to L1) with the streaming config, then F-D1 (gate and up as one launch with the SwiGLU epilogue)

levers.name: MLP streaming config and L1 multiply
levers.reason: F-D2: the 64-row MLP's multiply is written to L1 instead of DRAM and read from L1 by the down matmul; with a QWEN_FAST_MLP_CFG name (g<n>u<n>d<n>) the gate, up and down 1D-mcast matmuls are re-partitioned over more or fewer cores with the K loop (in0_block_w) unchanged, so every output tile is reduced over K as before

levers.name: MLP fused gate|up with SwiGLU epilogue
levers.reason: F-D1: the gate and up matmuls and their multiply become one launch (tp4_mlp_fused, a port of the TP2 FusedProjection to 64 rows and the TP4 shape, reading the served w1 and w3): the SiLU at the gate's pack, bf16 rounding of gate and up, a bf16 product left in L1 for the down matmul

image_files.reason: the levers' flags, config grammar, plan, twin forward, binder and audit; model_batch.two_tile_bindings imports it only when one of its flags is set
F-D1: the fused gate|up launch (host plan, compute-kernel patch, program descriptors); bindings() imports it on QWEN_FAST_MLP_GATEUP=1
JIT source of the fused launch's activation multicast; without it the fused arm fails at its first launch
JIT source of the fused launch's weight reader and output writer

tests.reason: flags, builder against the graft's transcription, the K-loop proofs, the twin forward beside the real grafted _forward_tp, the audit, the binder and the model_batch hook, the job templates
F-D1: the host plan, the compute patch against fused_1d.fused_compute, the kernels' data movement transliterated, the program descriptors
the card-M harness's own tests (a new directory; the workflow runs the sibling harness directories the same way)

card_jobs: scripts/ci/references/fusion-jobs/WP4/ (ORDER.txt; C1 the card-M sweep FIRST, C2 the same on the 11x10 clamp, C3 the fused op, C4 the other four 1D decode matmuls); the four-card audited attach and ABAB of the two levers come from make_fusion_jobs.py
notes: WP0 hooks, three lines each: (1) packed_verifier, beside tile_collective_tp.audit_claim / audit_replayed / audit_round / audit_release: tp4_mlp_gateup.audit_claim(fixture, 'warm' or 'capture') after the warm forward and after the capture, tp4_mlp_gateup.audit_replayed(fixture) after each replay, tp4_mlp_gateup.audit_round(operations, fixture, round_number) with the other audit rounds, tp4_mlp_gateup.audit_release(operations, fixture) before the fixture closes; with the audit flags off nothing is held and the calls return 0. Without them an audited arm logs no 'audit ... exact=True' line and the fusion smoke rule fails it by name. (2) scripts/ci/model_batch.py is edited by this branch: two_tile_bindings appends tp4_mlp_gateup.bindings(...) only when one of the five QWEN_FAST_MLP_* names is in the environment (the module is not imported otherwise; the overlay already lists model_batch). (3) Two more classifications this branch cannot make for itself: scripts/ci/test_tp4_closure_literals.py SERVED needs `tp4_mlp_gateup tp4_mlp_fused` (model_batch imports the first lazily and it imports the second; with them listed the test passes, scanned clean of pair literals), and c2_smoke_check can call tp4_mlp_gateup_smoke.problems(env, container_text) once per arm beside fusion_problems (host side, not shipped to the image: it adds the route and configuration name, rows=64, layers=64 and the L1 multiply to the generic fusion rules; without the call the generic rules still apply). (4) Not needed: tp_addresses rows (the lever binds an instance attribute per layer, no pinned module is twinned), profiles beyond the two levers (after card job C1 prints the tuned name, add {"name": "mlpcfg-tuned", "env": {"QWEN_FAST_MLP_CFG": "<name>"}, "audit": false} and its audited twin to profiles[] and regenerate). 13x10: nothing in the lever hard-codes a grid; the harness and the binder read compute_with_storage_grid_size, the sweep covers up to 130 cores, the fused op lays its workers on the device width.
